perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s available perspective:

- Sara knows she and Shirley Whiteplume are long-time colleagues and close friends at a community health center; Shirley is a nurse.
- Sara attended the funeral of a patient she and Shirley both knew. She saw Shirley looking somber and suspected Shirley was deeply affected by the loss.
- Sara heard Shirley say the loss had been tough and that she kept wondering if there was something more they could have done. Sara replied that they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought the patient. Shirley said Sara was right but it was hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, Sara raised the patient’s treatment decisions because she sensed Shirley felt burdened. She heard Shirley say she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have given him a better chance. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley appreciated it but said it was hard to accept.
- Sara observed Shirley continuing to be reserved and show little emotion. In a quiet office moment, Sara told Shirley she had noticed her holding back feelings and that it was okay to be open. Shirley said she wasn’t sure she could and didn’t want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotion doesn’t make her weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Later, Sara thought her earlier confrontation might have been too harsh. She apologized to Shirley. Shirley said it had been a bit much but knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley in whatever way needed. Shirley thanked her and said they should keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, Sara noticed Shirley seemed to be doing better. She asked how Shirley was feeling. Shirley said she was feeling better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara offered to spend more time together outside work. Shirley said she would like that and suggested planning something for the weekend.
